title: 10 Plants That Can K*ll You — You Probably Have No.3 at Home

scenes.text: Every year, thousands of people are poisoned... not by snakes... not by spiders... but by plants. Some look beautiful. Some taste sweet. And some are growing in gardens, parks, and homes all over the world... maybe even yours. Today, we're counting down ten plants that can kill you. And stay until number three... because there's a very good chance it's closer to you than you think.

scenes.name: JIMSONWEED
scenes.text: Number ten: Jimsonweed. In 1676, British soldiers sent to Jamestown, Virginia, boiled a strange green plant for a salad. What happened next was written into history. For eleven days, the men went completely mad. One blew feathers into the air. Another sat in a corner, grinning like a monkey. When they finally came back to their senses... they remembered nothing. The culprit? Datura, a common weed with a beautiful trumpet-shaped flower. Every part of it is loaded with toxins that can cause hallucinations, a racing heart... and death.

scenes.name: WHITE SNAKEROOT
scenes.text: Number nine: White Snakeroot. This one can kill you... without you ever touching it. In the early 1800s, a mysterious illness swept across the American frontier. People called it milk sickness, and thousands died. One of them, in 1818, was a woman named Nancy Hanks Lincoln... the mother of a nine-year-old boy named Abraham Lincoln. The cause was only understood much later. Cows were grazing on white snakeroot. The poison passed into their milk... and into the people who drank it.

scenes.name: FOXGLOVE
scenes.text: Number eight: Foxglove. Tall, purple, and found in cottage gardens everywhere. Foxglove contains chemicals that act directly on the heart. In tiny, controlled doses, they are medicine. Doctors have used digitalis to treat heart failure since 1785. But in the wrong dose, those same chemicals can throw the heart wildly out of rhythm... and then stop it. People have been poisoned simply by mistaking its leaves for harmless herbs, and brewing them into tea.

scenes.name: DEADLY NIGHTSHADE
scenes.text: Number seven: Deadly Nightshade. Its scientific name, belladonna, means beautiful woman in Italian, because in Renaissance Italy, women dropped its juice into their eyes to make their pupils huge and seductive. But its shiny black berries taste sweet... and that is the danger. Just a few can kill a child. Legend says that in the eleventh century, Scottish soldiers laced their enemies' drinks with it... then slaughtered the Danish army while it slept.

scenes.name: MONKSHOOD
scenes.text: Number six: Monkshood, known as the Queen of Poisons. Its hooded blue flowers hide aconitine, a toxin so strong it can be absorbed through the skin. Gardeners are warned to always wear gloves. In 2009, in London, a woman named Lakhvir Singh slipped Indian aconite into her former lover's curry. He never recovered. She was jailed for life... convicted by a plant that most people have never even heard of.

scenes.name: MANCHINEEL TREE
scenes.text: Number five: the Manchineel tree, listed by Guinness World Records as the most dangerous tree on Earth. Spanish explorers called its fruit the little apple of death. One bite can make your mouth and throat blister and swell. Its milky sap burns skin like acid. Even standing under it in the rain is dangerous, because the dripping water can carry that sap onto your skin. Burn the wood, and the smoke can damage your eyes. In Florida and the Caribbean, many of these trees are painted with red warning bands.

scenes.name: WATER HEMLOCK
scenes.text: Number four: Water Hemlock, often called the most violently toxic plant in North America. It looks like harmless wild parsley, growing peacefully beside streams. But its roots contain cicutoxin, which attacks the nervous system. In as little as fifteen minutes, victims can suffer violent seizures. In 1992, two brothers out foraging in Pennsylvania mistook it for wild ginseng. One of them took three bites of the root... and did not survive. Its close cousin, poison hemlock, is the plant that executed the philosopher Socrates.

scenes.name: OLEANDER
scenes.text: And number three... you have almost certainly seen it. Maybe even today. Oleander. Pink and white flowers. Glossy green leaves. It lines highways, school yards and parks, from Los Angeles to Lahore... and it sits in pots on millions of balconies. Every single part of it is poisonous. The leaves, the flowers, the stems, even the sap. Its toxins attack the heart, just like foxglove. Swallowing a single leaf can be enough to seriously poison a child. Even the smoke from burning it is dangerous. In Sri Lanka, the seeds of its cousin, yellow oleander, poison thousands of people every year. So the next time you walk past those pretty pink flowers... keep your hands away from your mouth.

scenes.name: CASTOR BEAN
scenes.text: Number two: the Castor Bean plant. Gardeners love its giant star-shaped red leaves. Factories press its seeds into castor oil, which is safe, because the poison stays behind. And that poison is ricin, one of the deadliest natural toxins known. In 1978, on London's Waterloo Bridge, a Bulgarian writer named Georgi Markov felt a sharp sting in his leg. A stranger with an umbrella had fired a tiny pellet into him, laced with ricin. Four days later... he was dead. And even today, there is no approved antidote for ricin.

scenes.name: ROSARY PEA
scenes.text: And number one... the Rosary Pea. Tiny, glossy, bright red seeds with a single black spot. They look like beads, and that is exactly how they are used. In bracelets, necklaces, and rosaries sold to tourists all over the world. But inside each seed is abrin, a toxin even deadlier than ricin. The hard shell protects you... as long as it stays unbroken. But if a seed is cracked or chewed, a single one may be enough to kill an adult. Jewelry made from these seeds has been pulled from shops because of this risk. So if you own a bracelet with little red and black beads... you might want to take a closer look.

Nature is beautiful... but it doesn't need claws or fangs to be deadly. Which of these plants have you seen near your home? Tell me in the comments. And if you want to see the most dangerous dogs in the world, watch this video next. Subscribe to Amazing Facts... and stay curious.
